title: Dispatch: Enforce prospective lifecycle admission against current campaign position (PR #524 review 3)
description:
Dispatch for PR #524 review #5097921608 (exact head 7c8eafe, semantic-system profile). The four defects from the previous review are CONFIRMED FIXED at this head. ONE blocking defect remains, independently reproduced by the supervisor before dispatch.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev3 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev3, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt at 7c8eafe (the reviewed head). npm ci has been run; @eshyra/core resolves into the worktree. verify:worktree now enforces this (PR #525). Work only inside that worktree.

=============================================================
DEFECT — ordinary lifecycle mutations can be backdated and rewrite canonical history
Owner: eshyra-jhpt.1 (temporal invariant) + eshyra-jhpt.2 (mutation boundary). Both are reopened.
=============================================================
eshyra-jhpt.1 permits exactly two temporal modes and excludes arbitrary historical retroactivity; .2 says ordinary rules apply prospectively with the disputed turn as the bounded exception. Neither is enforced against the campaign's CURRENT position.

campaignRules.ts checkTemporalMode returns immediately when mode === 'prospective', so currentPosition is never compared against a prospective rule's effectivePosition. The store then has no current-position authority of its own: revokeCampaignRule takes none at all, and create/supersede only compare a position against the rule's OWN effective position.

REPRODUCED at 7c8eafe (campaign current position P10 throughout):
  A. createCampaignRule effective P1 with validation.currentPosition = P10 -> ACCEPTED;
     historical active-at-position(P5) then reports [ 'backdated' ].
  B. revokeCampaignRule with revokedPosition P5 (no current-position input exists):
     active at P7 before: [ 'live' ]   after: [ ]                 <- history rewritten
  C. supersedeCampaignRule with a successor effective P5 and validation.currentPosition = P10:
     active at P7 before: [ 'old' ]    after: [ 'new' ]           <- historical set rewritten
  D. currentPosition can simply be OMITTED on create; nothing requires it.

TWO FACTS THAT SHAPE THE CORRECT FIX — verify them yourself, then use them:
  1. There are NO production callers of createCampaignRule / revokeCampaignRule / supersedeCampaignRule yet. Grep shows only the re-exports in src/internal.ts; eshyra-jhpt.5 will be the first real consumer. Making current-position authority REQUIRED is therefore a cheap breaking change that costs only test updates. Do it now rather than after .5 exists.
  2. The justification recorded on eshyra-jhpt.2.4 for allowing direct creation of non-active (superseded/revoked) rows was "so checkpoint/restore can rehydrate history". That justification does not hold: checkpoint restore does NOT use these APIs — persistence/checkpoint/store.ts materializes rows with raw `INSERT INTO` from the serialized snapshot. So the live mutation boundary can be made strict without breaking restore. Confirm this before relying on it.

REQUIRED PROPERTIES
  - The live mutation boundary must FAIL CLOSED without current-position authority. A caller must not be able to bypass the invariant by leaving currentPosition undefined. Preferred shape: make the current campaign position a REQUIRED argument of createCampaignRule, revokeCampaignRule and supersedeCampaignRule. An acceptable alternative is for the store to resolve the campaign's current canonical position itself from campaign_turn_position (which cannot be spoofed by a caller) — if you choose that, define and test the behaviour for a campaign with no turns yet. State which you chose and why.
  - Prospective creation must be rejected when effectivePosition precedes the current canonical position. Decide and document whether "at the current position" is permitted or only strictly after it; either is defensible, be explicit and test the boundary case.
  - Revocation must be rejected when revokedPosition precedes the current canonical position (in addition to the existing revokedPosition >= effectivePosition rule).
  - Supersession must be rejected when the successor's effectivePosition precedes the current canonical position (in addition to the existing successor >= prior rule).
  - The disputed-turn mode must KEEP working for the current or immediately preceding turn. Do not fix prospectivity by deleting the bounded retroactive exception — that mode is the whole point of eshyra-jhpt.8.
  - If a historical-row path is still wanted, make it a DISTINCT, explicitly named entry point that a caller cannot reach by accident, and say in your notes who is expected to use it. Given fact 2, consider whether it should exist at all.

REQUIRED PERMANENT EVIDENCE (the review names these; each must establish a LATER current position, which the existing tests never do)
  1. At current position P10, ordinary prospective creation backdated to P9 or earlier is rejected at the live storage boundary, the row set is unchanged, and historical active-at-position results are unchanged. Current/future prospective timing still works.
  2. A revocation backdated before the current canonical position is rejected, and the rule remains active in every historical slice the rejected mutation tried to change.
  3. A prospective supersession backdated before the current canonical position is rejected, preserving the prior rule, the supersession chain, and both historical and current active sets.
  4. The disputed-turn exception remains valid for the current and immediately preceding turn, and still rejects an older turn.
  5. Omitting current-position authority fails closed — prove the API cannot be called without it (a compile-time required argument counts, but add a runtime test for the resolved-from-DB case if you choose that design).
Note the existing tests named "applies supersession and revocation prospectively" and "rejects non-prospective lifecycle changes" only compare a transition against the rule's own effective position. They do not establish a later current position and so do not prove prospectivity in the contract sense. Strengthen them rather than leaving two tests whose names overstate what they check.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF: confirm each new regression fails against 7c8eafe (check the relevant source files out from that commit, observe failures, restore your fix). Report the counts you actually observed; do not infer them.
  - Do not weaken existing tests or assertions to accommodate the change. Updating test call sites for a newly required argument is expected and is not a weakening; silently relaxing an assertion is.
  - Do not change the active-at-position SQL predicate, the position encoding, merged migrations, the seam contract, or the four fixes from the previous review.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). Report final pass/skip counts and confirm @eshyra/core resolves into this worktree.
